title: Mommy Makeover Recovery: Week-by-Week Timeline and Checklist
meta_description: About 2 weeks off work, driving at 2 to 3 weeks, no lifting children for 4 to 6. A week-by-week mommy makeover recovery, a checklist and the warning signs.
excerpt: Here is what to expect from a mommy makeover recovery, week by week: how to plan around your kids, what to prepare before surgery, what is normal and which signs mean you should call your surgeon. Every figure names its source.
quick_answer:
How long is mommy makeover recovery?

The Aesthetic Society says to plan about 2 weeks off work, with someone else in charge of small children for at least 2 weeks. It puts driving at 2 to 3 weeks, heavy lifting at 4 to 6 weeks and strenuous activities at 6 weeks. Final results can take 6 months to a year (Frank Campanile, MD, ASPS website).

images.text_in_image:
Mommy makeover recovery, week by week
Day of surgery: You may be up and walking within hours. You cannot go home alone.
Within 5 days: Your first follow-up with your surgeon.
Week 1: The hardest week. After a tummy tuck, you stay bent at the waist for 7 to 10 days.
Weeks 2 to 3: You may be comfortable enough to drive now, or when your sutures and drains are out and you are off pain medication.
Weeks 4 to 6: No heavy lifting, such as picking up your children or baskets of laundry.
Week 6: You will probably need to wait until now before any strenuous activities.
Around 3 months: After a tummy tuck, swelling keeps going down until about now. You can usually return to your normal activities.
6 months to 1 year: Your final result.
6 months to 2 years: Scars fade and flatten.
Sources: The Aesthetic Society; Cindy Wu, MD, and Frank Campanile, MD, on the ASPS website. Your surgeon sets your own schedule.

images.alt: Card comparing normal recovery with reasons to call your surgeon after a mommy makeover. Usually normal: swelling and numbness that may take months to resolve, bruising and tenderness, pain in the first days, being bent at the waist for 7 to 10 days after a tummy tuck, not feeling like yourself for at least 7 to 10 days, still feeling like you are recovering for 2 to 3 weeks, bandages and compression garments. Call your surgeon: more swelling, pain, redness, drainage or bleeding, drainage that turns thick, tan, green or yellow or smells bad, extreme or lasting pain, an incision that looks larger, deeper, dried out or dark, a temperature above 100°F (37.7°C) for more than 4 hours, dizziness, nausea or vomiting, redness, warmth, swelling, pain or tenderness in a leg or arm. Chest pain, difficulty breathing, coughing up blood, fainting or loss of consciousness: go to the emergency room or call 911.

images.text_in_image:
What is normal after a mommy makeover, and when should you call your surgeon?
Usually normal | Call your surgeon
Swelling and numbness, which may take months to resolve | More swelling, pain, redness, drainage or bleeding
Bruising and tenderness early in recovery | Drainage that turns thick, tan, green or yellow, or smells bad
Pain in the first days, managed by pain medication | Pain that is extreme or lasts long
Being bent at the waist for 7 to 10 days after a tummy tuck | An incision that looks larger, deeper, dried out or dark
Not feeling like yourself for at least 7 to 10 days | A temperature above 100°F (37.7°C) for more than 4 hours
Still feeling like you are recovering for 2 to 3 weeks | Dizziness, nausea or vomiting
Bandages, compression garments and possibly surgical drains | Redness, warmth, swelling, pain or tenderness in a leg or arm
Go to the emergency room or call 911 for chest pain, difficulty breathing, coughing up blood, fainting or loss of consciousness.
Sources: The Aesthetic Society; MedlinePlus; Frank Campanile, MD, and Cindy Wu, MD, on the ASPS website.

sources.title: Mommy Makeover
quotes: The recovery time is at least two weeks but could be longer depending on your specific combination of procedures.
You can’t smoke. Smoking slows down the healing process and increases the risk of serious complications during and after surgery.
Pregnancy or weight gain following these surgeries may compromise your results.
You will likely have scars following these procedures hidden in your bikini line or under your bra.

sources.title: Mommy makeover: aftercare and recovery
quotes: When you combine procedures, the benefit is a single recovery time, but your recovery may be more intense. The first week will be the worst, and you may still feel like you are recovering for two to three weeks.

You may experience discomfort, swelling and numbness. You may be up and walking within hours of surgery, but you will need to recuperate for several weeks or longer, depending on how much surgery you undergo.
Plan to take about two weeks off from work, depending on the physical demands of your job.

The recovery period is significant and can be intense the first few days. You can speak with your surgeon about using a pain pump and medications to control pain and discomfort so that you can move about and sleep as needed.
The tummy tuck component of a “mommy makeover” is the most uncomfortable.

You won't feel like yourself for at least seven to ten days, and you still shouldn't do any heavy lifting (such as picking up your children or baskets of laundry) for four to six weeks. If you have small children, you must put someone else totally in charge of their care for at least two weeks.
You will likely go for a follow-up evaluation with your surgeon within five days. During this visit, your surgeon can remove the drainage tubes.

By the end of the first week, you should be walking around the house frequently, but you will still be unable to drive. You may be comfortable enough to drive a car in two or three weeks or when all of your sutures and drains are removed, and you are no longer taking pain medication.
If you have traditional sutures, you will typically have these removed within the first week or two (absorbable sutures will not have to be removed).
Make an effort to ease back into your normal routine gradually rather than all at once. You will probably need to wait six weeks after surgery before attempting any strenuous activities.
Swelling and numbness may take months to resolve.
Fading and flattening of scars take six months to two years.
When the anesthesia wears off, you may have some pain that can be managed by pain medication. If the pain is extreme or lasts long, contact your surgeon.
You can generally expect to wear bandages and compression garments, and you may have some surgical drains.
Arrange for someone to help you get around the house and help with your medication for at least the first 24 hours after surgery.

Ask your surgeon how to sleep, including the proper use of pillows to minimize the tension on your incisions, reduce pain and facilitate a thinner scar. Your surgeon may suggest you sleep with several pillows under your back and keep your legs slightly bent at the hips.
You will need to wear an abdominal binder after a tummy tuck. You may shower once the dressing, sponges, and gauze pads are removed. This usually occurs within 72 hours.

Call your surgeon immediately if you notice an increase in swelling, pain, redness, drainage, or bleeding in the surgical area or if you develop fever, dizziness, nausea, or vomiting. Other red flags include shortness of breath, chest pains, and unusual heartbeat.

sources.title: Mommy makeover: preparing for your procedure
quotes: Prepare meals that you can easily reheat. Stock your refrigerator before your surgery with high-protein, low-sodium foods, including fresh fruits and vegetables, and lots of caffeine-free beverages and water.
Store all the supplies you'll need during recovery where they're easily accessible (counter level, not in overhead or very low cabinets).
Stockpile items like your phone, charger, TV remote, your medication organizer, water, low-sodium crackers, tissues, and anything else you may need by your bed.
You should not be lifting, driving, doing laundry or cleaning during your recovery.
Establish a no-fail support system for the full recovery period. If you have children less than five years of age, you must have someone take care of them for at least the first two weeks.
Pick items that open in front. Wear slip-on shoes so you don't have to bend.
Avoid taking aspirin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications (NSAIDs: Advil, Motrin, Aleve), and vitamins/homeopathic regimens that can increase bleeding.

Whether your surgery is an inpatient or outpatient procedure and whether you stay overnight at a recovery center depends on many variables, including your medical issues, the number of procedures you will undergo, the length of time your surgery takes, and the availability of your caregiver at home.
If you go home the same day, be sure to arrange for someone to drive you home after surgery and to stay with you for several days following surgery.
Under no circumstances will you be permitted to go home alone or stay home without another adult present.

sources.title: What to expect during your mommy makeover recovery
quotes: However, most women plan to take about two weeks away from work to rest and recover at home. Plan to enlist some help from another adult during this time, as you'll need to avoid lifting anything heavy, including your children.
During this initial stage of recovery, you can expect to have some swelling, bruising and tenderness as your body heals.
Usually, around the three-month mark, you can return to your normal activities, although it can take six months to a year before you see your final mommy makeover results.
Now is not the time to worry about dieting or losing weight.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Cindy Wu, MD
sources.title: Answers to common tummy tuck questions
quotes: You will be bent at the waist while standing or lying down for 7-10 days after surgery to protect the incision and to allow for your skin to adapt.
If a drain is placed, then it will be removed as soon as the output is low enough (usually in 1-2 weeks).

You can walk the day of surgery. In fact, most plastic surgeons encourage patients to walk three times the day of surgery to improve blood circulation to keep the risk of blood clots in the legs to a minimum. However, running or lifting should be avoided for six weeks after the procedure.

The bruising will subside in a couple of weeks, and the swelling will continue to diminish until approximately three months post-procedure. The scars will continue to heal and will become thinner and lighter in color at around 12-18 months.

quotes: If you have young children, you will want to enlist help to assist with childcare, as squatting or picking up children (or heavy objects for that matter) for the first few weeks is strongly advised against.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Paul Vitenas, Jr., MD
sources.title: Five things to consider before getting a tummy tuck
quotes: In most cases, the drains are painlessly removed in seven to ten days, however, they may need to stay in place for two weeks or longer.

sources.title: Surgical wound care – closed
quotes: Contact your surgeon if there are any of the following changes around the incision:
More redness or pain
Swelling or bleeding
The wound is larger or deeper
The wound looks dried out or dark
You should also contact your surgeon if the drainage coming from or around the incision increases or becomes thick, tan, green, or yellow, or smells bad (pus).
Also contact your surgeon if your temperature is above 100°F (37.7°C) for more than 4 hours.

sources.title: Deep venous thrombosis
quotes: Redness of the skin
Skin that feels warm to the touch
Swelling (edema) of a leg or arm
Pain or tenderness in a leg or arm
Contact your provider if you have symptoms of DVT.
Go to the emergency room or call the local emergency number (such as 911) if you have DVT and you develop:
Chest pain
Coughing up blood
Difficulty breathing
Fainting
Loss of consciousness

sources.title: Mommy Makeovers: How They Work and What To Expect
quotes: Often, surgeons recommend no heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for the first four to six weeks.
You’ll need to quit smoking for at least six weeks prior to surgery.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar
quotes: Avoid heavy lifting, strenuous exercise, sexual activity and stretching until your provider says it’s safe to do these activities (usually four to eight weeks after the procedure).
For 12 to 18 months after your tummy tuck, wear sunscreen with an SPF (sun protection factor) of 30 if you have to be in the sun.
